newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch closing share market report.
newsitem.headline: Dutch closing share market report.

text.p: Dutch shares closed higher on Wednesday, recovering all of Tuesday's losses and heading back towards 620 on the AEX, pulled higher by a strong overnight Wall Street performance and helped by a firm dollar.

Dealers said Wall Street's higher opening on Wednesday gave impetus in the last hour of Amsterdam trading to a market already comfortably higher on the day. But traders said business had been very slow and prices had been squeezed as investors who had recently sold short attempted to cover their positions.
The AEX closed 5.49 points higher at 618.43, its high on the day and 22 points up since touching 595.82 last Friday.

"Today's gain is backed by the move on Wall Street last night and the steady dollar and the lack of negative news out of the bond market," said one dealer. "The turnover is just not there though. It looks like people are doing some year-end tidying up, it's just stock picking at the moment."
Another dealer said the thinness of trade had exaggerating the upward movements, which were partly influenced by pressure out of the options market.
"This gain has everthing to do with low volume and shortage of stock," he said.

"The market did OK of course after the decision of the Fed yesterday not to raise interest rates. We were about four points up before the Wall Street opening so we went again when they opened higher," said another dealer.
Some dealers felt that the market seemed to be regaining its poise after recent comments from Fed chairman Alan Greenspan that triggered talk of a U.S. rate rise.

"If you look at what's happened since Greenspan's remarks we've come a long way back up. It's looking as though the dip caused by Greenspan was way overdone and people are now picking up stock to cover short positions here and there," he said.
Another dealer said index call options expiring at 620, taken out before Greenspan's remarks on December 6, had come back into demand and were helping fuel the cash market rise.
"There was a lot of public options buying because of the rally (before Greenspan) and that's built in a lot of premium around 620," he said.

Some dealers, however, were mistrustful of the day's rise. "Today's gains were on really low volume and that's not a good sign. People who are into the market already are scared and waiting to sell, they're still hoping for a move up then they are likely to start selling immediately."

The market yielded few features although Royal Dutch added 3.10 guilders to 291.50 and Philips rose 1.00 guilder to 69.00. The company said it would phase out production of lamps at Little Rock, Arkansas and that it was planning to cut jobs at its liquid crystal display unit in Eindhoven.
Financials were higher with ING 80 cents higher at 58.90 guilders and ABN AMRO 1.50 guilders up at 107.80.
